instrument: Prakriti Parikshan (Vata / Pitta / Kapha) - 40 item, Govardhan School of Yoga YTT workbook
source: Adapted from the 'Prakriti Parikshan' Ayurvedic Constitution Self-Assessment workbook (Govardhan School of Yoga, Yoga Teacher Training). Original items, not a reproduction of the copyrighted CCRAS Prakriti Assessment Scale. Five sections: Body Structure (Sharira), Digestion/Sleep/Energy (Ahara-Nidra-Bala), Mind and Temperament (Manas), Lifestyle and Preferences (Vihara), On the Mat (Abhyasa). Each item is a forced choice between three dosha-characteristic answers, labelled A/B/C to the user; dosha labels are not shown while answering.

response_scale.note: Each item has exactly 3 options, one per dosha. Users normally tick one option; ticking two (when equally true) is allowed but should be rare. One ticked option = 2 points to that dosha. Two ticked options on the same item = 1 point each to those two doshas. No option text should contain the words Vata, Pitta, or Kapha.

dimensions.VAT: Vata - Air + Space, light, quick, variable
dimensions.PIT: Pitta - Fire + Water, sharp, warm, intense
dimensions.KAP: Kapha - Earth + Water, heavy, steady, slow

vikriti_check.instrument: Current State Check (Vikriti) - 6 item, distinct from Prakriti above
vikriti_check.note: Same three-column structure but answered for the last 4-6 weeks only, not lifelong pattern. Measures which dosha is currently disturbed rather than constitution. Score = count of ticked items per column, out of 6 each.

options.text: Waking hot or around 2 a.m. with a busy mind
Low motivation, feeling stuck or dull
Being overly critical of self or others

vikriti_check.interpretation: Vikriti matching Prakriti (e.g. a Pitta type with Pitta symptoms) means the dominant dosha has increased - the most common pattern. Vikriti differing from Prakriti (e.g. a Kapha type with Vata symptoms) means lifestyle, season, travel or stress is pulling the person away from their nature; address the current imbalance first. Three or more ticks in any column is worth attention; four or more in several columns, or anything persistent, warrants referral to a qualified Ayurvedic physician rather than self-treatment.

scoring_notes: 40 items across 5 sections (9+12+8+6+5), 80 points total. Each item: one ticked option = 2 points to that dosha; two ticked options (allowed sparingly, when equally true) = 1 point each. Sum points per dosha, convert to percentage of 80. Classification (apply in order, stop at first match): (1) Sama/Tridoshaja - all three percentages within 10 points of each other; rare, re-check before accepting. (2) Ekadoshaja (single dosha) - the highest dosha leads the second by 15 points or more. (3) Dvandvaja (dual dosha) - otherwise; name the higher of the top two first (e.g. Vata-Pitta). Boundary results within 2-3 points should be read against both candidate profiles. The Vikriti check (see vikriti_check) is a separate, short-term instrument scored independently and should be interpreted alongside but never merged into the Prakriti percentages.
